findings.title: UsernameForm calls a no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that does not exist
findings.body: Line 47 calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only method with that name is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java line 160); neither UsernameForm nor any superclass in the changed files defines a no-arg overload, so this class does not compile. If a no-arg overload is added, it must return whether passkeys are enabled independently of the current user, otherwise the initial login page stays broken (see the UsernamePasswordForm finding).

findings.title: Null-user guard disables conditional passkey UI on the initial login page
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` (line 161) returns false when `user == null`, and it is used at lines 115 and 137 to decide whether to call `fillContextForm`. `fillContextForm` is what sets `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`, the WebAuthn challenge, RP ID, user-verification, etc. Since `context.getUser()` is null on the initial username/password page and on invalid-username errors, the conditional passkey autofill/`#webauth` form is no longer rendered there. Previously `fillContextForm` was called exactly in the `user == null` branch, so this swap inverts the behavior. Consequence: the username field loses `autocomplete="username webauthn"`, discoverable-key automatic login on the first page stops working, and unchanged tests fail (e.g. PasskeysUsernameFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey lines 183-190, PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest lines 145-146, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest lines 192-194). `fillContextForm` should run whenever passkeys are enabled, regardless of whether a user is already set.

findings.title: Unused NoSuchElementException import after replacing assertThrows
findings.body: The diff removes the only two usages of `NoSuchElementException` (the `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` calls) but leaves the import on line 51. Keycloak's checkstyle rejects unused imports, so the build will fail unless the import is removed.

findings.title: Unused PasswordCredentialModel import
findings.body: `PasswordCredentialModel` is imported on line 35 but never referenced in the file (the tests use `WebAuthnCredentialModel` and `getPassword`). This would be flagged/failed by checkstyle as an unused import.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey does not test a user without a passkey
findings.body: The test name and intent say it covers a user who has no passkey, but `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` disables passkeys for the whole realm, which is a different code path (`WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.isPasskeysEnabled` returns false and `fillContextForm` is never invoked). The new code only checks the realm policy, not whether the re-authenticating user actually has a passkey, so a user with only a password would still be shown the passkey UI during re-authentication. Add a case that keeps passkeys enabled for the realm and re-authenticates a user that has no passkey credential, to verify the expected fallback to password (especially for the UsernameForm flow).
